question: [PRACTICE] What will the average "new forecasters per day" be on this question before this question closes?

calls.reasoning: Identified the question as Metaculus post 45516 in the Fall 2026 FutureEval Bot Tournament: 128 forecasters shown as of 2026-09-13, with only 1 new forecaster in the past week, so the close-date numerator is ~129-145. The answer is therefore almost entirely a days-open question. Fall 2026 tournament questions were already resolving by Aug 31, 2026, and Summer's practice set went live ~2-3 weeks before that season's May 18 start, which argues for a late-August (or earlier) open and D in the 30s-40s; the fast saturation-then-silence accrual curve and the tournament's own bot aggregate (~5.3, implying D~25) argue for an open around Sep 1-4. The 'only 1 this week' line also rules out a very recent open, capping the value near ~6. I split the difference, centering on D~31 days (open ~Aug 28) with a left tail for an early-August open and a right tail for a Sep 3-6 open. No prediction market prices anything resembling this; evidence on the open date is genuinely thin and I stayed near the reference-class anchor.

calls.reconciliation: DISPUTE 1 (factual, SETTLED-CONFIRMED): the observed state. All three runs reported 128 forecasters, '1 this week', 0 comments, and an on-page estimate near 5.29. My own proxy fetch of the live page returned exactly these figures plus the 2.7-7.5 interval. No dispute survives. DISPUTE 2 (factual, UNRESOLVED - checked and came back empty): the open date of post 45516. I fetched the question page and the API both directly and through a text-extraction proxy; the direct routes returned HTTP 403 and the proxied API route returned an explicit 'API is only available to authenticated users' message. Two web searches for a Fall 2026 FutureEval announcement or for post 45516 returned nothing referencing either. Every run's blocked-access report is confirmed; the date must stay inferred. DISPUTE 3 (judgment, the real disagreement): D. Run 1 said ~31 days (open ~Aug 28), inferring an early open from Fall-feed questions resolving Aug 31 and from Summer's 2-3 week practice lead; Runs 2 and 3 said ~25-26. I side with the shorter window, and the reason is a constraint Run 1 did not weigh: post IDs are allocated monotonically at creation, and a post cannot open before it is created. Run 2's interpolation anchors (notebook 43340 = May 1 2026; post 45606 = ~Sep 11 2026, ~17 IDs/day) place 45516's creation around Sep 3-6, which is a hard ceiling on how early it could have opened - Run 1's Aug 28 would require the ID rate in that stretch to fall to roughly a quarter of the seasonal average, and MiniBench's 60-question batch injections bias the local rate faster, not slower. I could not independently verify the 45606 anchor (the API is gated), so I do not treat it as airtight, which is why I keep left-tail mass out to D~38 rather than truncating at 28. Running the other way, the trailing-week silence rules out anything after ~Sep 5, since a Sep 6+ open would put all 127 arrivals inside the week the UI reports as 1. The two constraints together give D ~24-28, median 27 - between Run 1 and Run 2 not by splitting the difference but because each side supplies a bound and they nearly meet. Run 2's worry that a Sep 3 open is incompatible with the silence dissolves once you note the metric counts UNIQUE forecasters: a standing cron-driven bot roster exhausts itself in 1-3 days, after which the counter flattens by construction. DISPUTE 4 (judgment): the numerator. Run 3's ~130 assumes essentially no further inflow; Run 2's ~145 prices a pre-season surge. Run 2 has the better of this - the Summer analog (post 43339) shows a mass of bot activity the day before that season opened, and this question closes exactly at the Fall season start, so the same mechanism is pointed at the final week here. I carry 130-175, median ~140, nearer Run 2 but below its 185 ceiling since this question has drawn 0 comments against the analog's 342 and is a discrete rather than binary question. DISPUTE 5 (judgment): how much to lean on the on-page 5.29. Run 2 sat above it, Run 1 read it as implying D~25, Run 3 ignored it. I ignored it as an anchor - it is a bot-only aggregate the harness classes as unvalidated, and every bot producing it faces the same blocked open date I do, so it carries no information I lack. That my independent 140/27 lands at 5.2 is a coincidence worth noting, not an input I used. DISPUTE 6 (factual, SETTLED): market existence. All three runs and the harness found nothing; my own check adds no contract. 'None found' is confirmed. On escape mass: I declare only p_above_upper, at 1%, since clearing 10.05 needs F>220 at the shortest defensible D - far past the 156-forecaster analog. I dropped Runs 2 and 3's p_below_lower entirely: falling under 0.95 requires D>145 days, i.e. an open in late April 2026, which the post-ID ordering (notebook 43340 was published May 1 at ID ~43340) makes arithmetically impossible.
